text:
jun: Heads up — I’m seeing correlated spikes in /chat/compose p99 token latency whenever MIG slice 'slice-2' exceeds ~85C and kvcache eviction rate jumps. Put the new perf rollup on the screen and you can see the stair-step.

maria: link? can you post the panel or the query? :eyes:

jun: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/rt-abc/mig-thermal-kvcache?orgId=1

jun: quick summary:
- route: /chat/compose
- symptom: token_latency_p99_ms rising from ~120ms -> 480ms during 09:12–09:18 window
- coincident: gpu_temp_c (slice-2) climbs 78 -> 87C
- coincident: kvcache_evictions_total 5m rate jumps 0.2 -> 3.4

alex: ok can we get the exact PromQLs so we can stitch into a composite panel? here are the queries i used locally:
```
# route p99 token latency (per-route histogram)
sum by(route) (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)))

# kvcache eviction rate for slice-2, route
sum(rate(kvcache_evictions_total{slice="slice-2",route="/chat/compose"}[5m]))

# avg GPU temp for slice-2
avg_over_time(gpu_temp_c{slice="slice-2"}[5m])
```

maria: nice. any kernel selector correlation? like did we fall back to slower kernels when temp rises?

alex: saw a handful of kernel fallback events around the same window — driver logs show more small-SM occupancy kernels being chosen. snippet from runtime logs:
```
[09:13:42] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel="matmul_tiled_v2", fallback_reason="thermal_rebalance"
[09:13:42] sm_occupancy: 12.3% -> 8.9% (slice-2)
```

tara: metrics-bot flagged an alert at 09:15: "route_chat_compose_token_p99 > 400ms" — deploy-bot triggered autoscale but the autoscaler put new work on the same MIG slice group which was already thermal-limited.

metrics-bot: Alert: route_chat_compose_token_p99 (route="/chat/compose") exceeded threshold. value=478ms, window=5m. tags=[mig=slice-2]

deploy-bot: Autoscaling triggered: +2 pods to pool gpu-mig-slice-2-pool

jun: that’s the crux — autoscaler didn't circuit to different MIG pools. we need a routing policy that prefers non-thermal-limited pools for latency SLO routes.

maria: short-term mitigation options? reduce batch target, increase kvcache size, or steer route off slice-2.

alex: agreed. quick checklist I ran through:
- reduce dynamic_batcher.target_batch_size for /chat/compose from 256 -> 192 (should reduce tail due to queuing)
- temporarily increase kvcache.max_entries for slice-2 route to reduce evictions
- add routing override: prefer pool tag="high-latency-safe" when gpu_temp_c > 80

jun: i pushed a config change to try the batch reduction in canary for 10 minutes. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/+/refs/changes/987

tara: I’ll scope an emergency route policy: if avg(gpu_temp_c{slice!=""}) > 82 for 5m, set routing priority to avoid that pool for SLO routes. will open a ticket.

maria: can we add a composite dashboard that shows a 3-axis correlation (kvcache_evictions, gpu_temp_c, route_token_p95/p99) and a heatmap per-mig-slice? that’ll help product and SRE triage.

alex: working on a panel template. suggestion for a heatmap query:
```
# normalized correlation matrix per slice (5m)
correlate_over_time(5m, [
  "sum(rate(kvcache_evictions_total[5m])) by (slice)",
  "avg_over_time(gpu_temp_c[5m]) by (slice)",
  "sum by(slice) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, slice)))"
])
```
(placeholder function — will implement via Grafana transformations)

jun: nice. immediate action items:
- alex -> finish and merge batch-size canary (PR above) and add quick rollback (ETA 15m)
- tara -> create routing rule ticket + emergency rule (ETA 30m)
- maria -> add composite dashboard panel and share snapshot (ETA 1h)
- jun -> monitor for next 6 hours, if p99 doesn't drop open paging incident

maria: copying eng-ml to see if model behavior could be contributing (longer decode patterns triggering kvcache churn). @alex can you grab a sample trace for /chat/compose from 09:10–09:20 and redact prompts?

alex: will do. pulling trace now; will sanitize and drop into the incident folder.

tara: re: long-term: we should consider kvcache backpressure to avoid eviction storms under thermal pressure (e.g., prioritize keeping recent prefixes for SLO routes). filing an RFC after the triage.

jun: thanks everyone. keep updates here. :thumbsup:
